answers.ask: How tall should the tower be, and how many stages?
answers.answer: Make it a small, clearly climbable tower with 10 stages, leading up to the playground and restart portal at the top.

answers.ask: How many this-or-that choice points, and does the choice change the route or just get recorded?
answers.answer: Use one this-or-that choice point per stage, with two short routes based on the selected satisfying ASMR object; both routes rejoin before the next stage.

scene_prompt: Create a 3D ASMR-themed obby tower: a small, clearly climbable vertical tower with 10 stacked stages made from satisfying-looking objects. Each stage contains one this-or-that choice point splitting into two short routes themed around different ASMR objects, then rejoining before the next stage. Place large screens playing ASMR videos at the bottom and at the top of the tower. The summit opens onto a playground area with cool items and a restart portal.
agent_notes: The prompt says tower obby, so Obby & Platformer leads on its genre-wide P6 and course-tower with the Tower Obby preset is the shape; ASMR sound, satisfying music and the on-screen chat are audio and UI rather than layout, so they change nothing spatial and no second genre is doing real work. The author's answer makes each of the ten stages a this-or-that fork whose two short routes rejoin, which I carried as obstacle-guess with its text bent to a paired-door choice where neither pick is punished, since nothing else in the catalogue expresses a two-way branch. The restart portal at the summit is teleporter-link, the playground and cool items at the top are winner-zone, and the two big ASMR video screens are folded into geometry that already exists: the lower one into social-hub as the gathering lobby at the tower base, the upper one into the winner-zone playground. Stage count is ten and the tower is deliberately small and climbable, both taken from the answers; the stated ten has no field to live in here, so it is recorded in this note.
